title: Find the bottom of the bowl, and check it with right angles
brief: Write the squared-miss loss and its gradient, solve the normal equations, then measure how far a fit is from perpendicular, project the targets onto the column space, and decide when a fit is the best one.
hints: loss: misses = X @ w - y, then 0.5 * np.sum(misses ** 2). Return a float.
gradient: X.T @ (X @ w - y). The result has one entry per weight, so its shape is (d,).
fit_normal_equations: np.linalg.solve(X.T @ X, X.T @ y). Do not invert the matrix.
residual_orthogonality: r = y - X @ w, then float(np.abs(X.T @ r).max()).
project: the fitted values are X @ fit_normal_equations(X, y), which has shape (n,), not (d,).
is_best_fit: compare residual_orthogonality(X, y, w) with tol * np.abs(X.T @ y).max().
